todo_line: - [ ] 004 Implement and test explicit custom-group-removal follow cleanup through public Messaging APIs, including manual and auto-follow sources, idempotent stale-safe remove/re-add ordering, unrelated-follow preservation, and unchanged system-group behaviour.
outcome: Finish task 004 by ensuring only authoritative action boundaries can attach source-group causality to a follow, and prove the surviving-group root path captures that causality through the production current-member send API.
scope: Revise the existing unaccepted task-004 candidate in place. Preserve its current structure while addressing the latest review gap: group-specific cleanup cutoffs, no phantom follow for an initially unfollowed shared conversation, historic replay compatibility, cleanup checkpoint barrier, idempotency, and source-aware manual/root/reply follow ordering.

Remove the trust boundary violation in `Memba.Messaging.follow_conversation/2` and its private command builder. Raw public callers must not be able to supply `authorizing_group_ids` as trusted causal provenance. Keep raw/system follows conservative, while `follow_conversation_as_current_member/2` continues to derive current readable groups authoritatively.

Preserve trusted source capture for sender auto-follow: root sends derive the selected audience at the service boundary, replies derive current writable conversation groups, and `establish_message_sender_follow/1` carries the committed source groups into `FollowConversation`.

Add a regression for removal from group A at generation G followed by a raw public follow attempt that claims arbitrary/non-authorizing group B. Prove the attempt emits no `ConversationFollowed`, creates no projected follow, and does not resume notifications when A is later re-added; a new authorized post-re-add follow must still restore normal following.

Replace the direct `Messaging.App.dispatch(%SendMessage{})` proof in the same-generation surviving-group root case with `Memba.Messaging.send_club_message_as_current_member/2`. Prove the production boundary authorizes active group B and records B in both `MessageSent.sender_follow_group_ids` and the resulting `ConversationFollowed.authorizing_group_ids` at the unchanged club generation.

Rerun the focused task-004 suites to preserve stale removed-group rejection, surviving-group manual/reply behavior, genuine post-re-add following, unrelated-follow preservation, cleanup retry, replay/idempotency, system-group no-ops, and accepted task-001 removal behavior.
scope_exclusions: Do not change task identity 004 or discard any of its five cumulative candidate origins.

Do not redesign `FollowConversation`, `ConversationFollowed`, `ConversationFollowers`, member follow eligibility, cleanup facts, projections, or historic absent-field replay unless a focused regression demonstrates that a minimal compatibility adjustment is required.

Do not make arbitrary raw callers trusted by validating only UUID shape. Non-empty causal source groups must come from an authoritative application boundary or an explicitly isolated trusted internal path.
Do not weaken the effective-access union: a genuine follow through surviving group B remains valid at group A's removal generation, while work sourced only from removed A remains rejected.
Do not change accepted task-001 custom-group removal authorization, transition/idempotency semantics, club roles or membership, or system-group guards.
Do not implement the broader query/action authorization, LiveView refresh, or queued provider-handoff work assigned to tasks 009-011.
Do not implement Leave/Remove UI, shared member-row changes, confirmations, post-removal surfaces, or empty-group presentation assigned to tasks 012-014.
Do not edit iteration-064 feature files or implement the remaining browser/domain acceptance layer assigned to tasks 015-016.
Do not run `dev check`, `dev check --quick`, `dev ci`, browser acceptance, or another unscoped full-suite command; task 017 and the deterministic `dev_check` node own the final repository gate.

references.facts: Implementation Plan 2 and the acceptance/open-technical-decision text require public Messaging APIs, all follow sources, stale remove/re-add safety, explicit re-follow after re-add, and durable cross-context ordering.
Iteration 062 established the replay-safe Membership-to-Messaging cleanup collaboration that explicit removal extends.
Membership owns group membership, Messaging owns follow state, and collaboration crosses public context APIs rather than projection storage or foreign aggregate internals.
The Club stream is authoritative for membership lifecycle and preserves historic facts; system-group membership remains a policy-maintained consequence.

`follow_conversation_command/1` currently copies caller-provided `authorizing_group_ids`, while `follow_conversation_as_current_member/2`, `send_club_message_as_current_member/2`, `post_message_reply/2`, and `establish_message_sender_follow/1` are the existing authoritative source-capture paths.
`follow_allowed?/4` trusts any supplied uncut source group after validating only UUID shape, so an arbitrary source supplied through the raw builder bypasses the removed-group cutoff.

The current same-generation test covers authoritative manual/reply paths but proves the root case by direct `Messaging.App.dispatch/2`; extend it with the forged-source regression and route the root through the production current-member send API.
Existing current-member send tests establish the production authorization contract and should remain passing.
Commands and events are write authority; projections must not decide or manufacture trusted follow causality.
Ordering and replay behavior must remain represented in durable backward-compatible facts.
Use deterministic synchronization and state/barrier assertions rather than timing sleeps.

constraints: Keep the same pending obligation and revision identity; this is attempt six for task 004.

Raw `follow_conversation/2` must not map untrusted caller attributes into `FollowConversation.authorizing_group_ids`. Ignoring the unsupported key is preferred over broadening the public error contract unless existing repository behavior requires explicit rejection.
Non-empty source attribution must be derived from authoritative current read/write membership or from a committed message event whose source was captured at that authoritative boundary.
After remove A at generation G, a raw attempt claiming B must remain blocked by conservative conversation-wide ordering; re-adding A must not make that rejected attempt effective.
After a genuine re-add advances membership generation, an explicit authorized current-member follow remains allowed and is the operation that restores notification eligibility.
The surviving-B root regression must call `send_club_message_as_current_member/2`, not build or dispatch `SendMessage` directly.
Preserve cleanup checkpoint synchronization, per-group cutoffs, ordinary-unfollow cutoff history, completed cleanup IDs, public add/remove return modes, and historic event replay.
Keep edits narrowly limited to the trusted source-attribution boundary, focused tests, and any directly necessary documentation comments.
completion_evidence_required: List changed paths and identify the builder/boundary change that prevents raw caller attributes from becoming trusted `authorizing_group_ids` while preserving authoritative manual/root/reply source capture.
Identify the regression proving remove A, forged raw source B, and re-add A produce no `ConversationFollowed`, projected follow, or reply delivery until a new authorized post-re-add follow.

Identify the production-path root test proving `send_club_message_as_current_member/2` records surviving group B in `MessageSent.sender_follow_group_ids` and `ConversationFollowed.authorizing_group_ids` at the unchanged removal generation.

Confirm the prior initially-unfollowed shared cleanup, retained shared follow, stale A versus surviving B manual/reply paths, genuine post-re-add follow, unrelated follow, cleanup retry, checkpoint interleaving, replay/idempotency, and Everyone/Admin regressions remain passing.
Report exact exit statuses and test counts for both focused test commands, plus `git diff --check`, on the handoff state.

Confirm accepted task-001 behavior remains unchanged: a real explicit removal emits only the reusable Membership removal fact, an exact retry emits no new Membership fact, and club roles/membership plus system-group guards are preserved.
